page: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g is a dedicated compute instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute series. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 16 vCPUs configured across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 64 GB, establishing a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per virtual CPU. The underlying CPU topology includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set coverage includes modern vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, accompanied by hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Performance testing reveals a divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. In single-core workloads, the instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core benchmarks, single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench text processing, ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Small-model LLM generation (135M model) also demonstrates top-tier speed at 418.37 tokens per second. In contrast, multi-threaded benchmarks place the machine in the middle 50 percent, with a PassMark CPU score of 34,362.3 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,761.0. Memory throughput remains solid, scoring in the top 25 percent on PassMark with an uncached large-block read speed of 88.72 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs center primarily around local storage and acceleration. The server lacks dedicated GPUs and includes only 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, functioning essentially as a minimal boot volume that necessitates attached network block storage for persistent application data. Because virtual CPUs are fully dedicated rather than shared, the hardware profile avoids noisy-neighbor performance degradation. Given its balanced resource ratios and strong single-thread execution, the vx1-g-16c-64g is suited for continuous integration runners, compilation tasks, web serving layers, and microservices backends.
description: The Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g is a general-purpose cloud instance in the VX1 Cloud Compute family, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs from an 8-core AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz paired with 64 GB of memory. It features a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio, 32 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16. Benchmark performance highlights exceptional single-threaded compute, text processing, and compression throughput within the top 10 percent tier, while multi-core operations perform at the median average. Bundled storage is limited to a minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD, and no GPUs are included. With dedicated CPU allocation and strong memory bandwidth, the instance is engineered for application backends, software compilation pipelines, web servers, and distributed microservices.
